title: Knowledge base state at start
detail: knowledge base: llm router, 0 tests, 0 findings, 0 wiki pages
note: ~/.skydiscover/llm-router does not exist: cold knowledge base, fresh discovery required. Nothing to reuse.

title: Run mode: headless autonomous
detail: No human available; every open question is answered by declared default, else by the lead with recorded reasoning.
note: User directive in the /skysynth invocation. Iteration budget fixed at 30 by the user, so the Step 4 budget question is not asked.

title: What may the router use to judge how well each candidate model would answer a given request?
detail: only signals a deployed router could observe at request time
note: Determined by the shipped baseline, not a free choice: evaluator/generic_policy.py:60 scores with a precomputed prediction head keyed by req.features['prompt_id'] (evaluator/benchmark/artifacts/generic_predictions.json), never req.quality. Reading the ground-truth req.quality dict the harness grades with would make the specialist an unreachable oracle and beat the baseline on information, not policy: a reward hack. Router code may read req.features and req.slo only.

title: May a tenant's router take capacity on the shared fleet that the other tenant would otherwise have used?
detail: yes, up to whatever the provider's published limits allow
note: Default taken, and the harness makes it non-adversarial: evaluator/benchmark/replay_tenants.py replays ONE tenant trace at a time (trace_tenantA_val.jsonl / trace_tenantB_val.jsonl), so no specialist can observe or starve the other tenant inside a scored replay. Self-imposed headroom would only handicap; published provider limits remain the binding constraint.

title: How freely may the router serve a different model from the one the request named, given that the request permits it?
detail: serve whichever model in the permitted set looks best on quality against price for this request
note: SETTLED BY THE MEASURED TRACE, not a default. All 6,504 train+val rows carry downgrade_ok:true and one identical equiv_class of all 12 models, so the permitted set is the whole fleet on every request. On the measured score/cost matrices the requested model is dominated for tenant A: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 scores 0.5350 vs gpt-5's 0.5113 on val (0.5254 vs 0.4950 on train) at $0.002418 vs $0.025722 per request, a static utility of 0.5277 vs 0.4342. Fleet cost spread is 15.3-20.8x on A traffic and 112.7-123.4x on B traffic, so with the objective's -3.0*cost weight substitution is the widest single lever. cards/workload.json dimensions.quality_cost_landscape.

title: Among the providers that stock the chosen model, what decides which one gets the request?
detail: remaining allowance and expected time-to-answer weighed together
note: declared default

title: When no provider can serve a request right now, does the router wait for capacity or refuse the request?
detail: wait for capacity, with an explicit point at which the router gives up
note: declared default

title: How long may a request that cannot be served yet keep waiting before the router stops waiting on it?
detail: until its own deadline runs out, and no longer
note: SETTLED BY THE MEASURED TRACE. A single fixed patience is provably wrong for one of the two tenants: A's whole budget is 2,500 ms from arrival while B's median queue slack is 532 s and its p90 is 391 s, and B's waves need 109-190 s of whole-fleet drain time that only deadline-length patience makes room for. Both tenants carry a deadline on every row (measured: 100% coverage, no row without an slo field), so tying patience to the request's own deadline is always defined. cards/workload.json dimensions.deadline_feasibility_headroom.

title: How should the router stay inside a provider's published request and token allowance?
detail: subtract the request's own expected consumption from the published remaining allowance before dispatching
note: SETTLED BY THE MEASURED TRACE. Learning from a rejection is unaffordable for tenant A: a 429 costs a fixed 2,000 ms of a 2,500 ms budget, after which only prime can still land and only for prompts under 6,000 tokens, so 6.28% of A val rows (61/972, every tau2 row) can never recover from one throttle. The rejections are real, not hypothetical: A's val peak offers 181 requests per 60 s against prime's rpm 132 (137%) and courier's 150 (121%), and the env card records 19.4% of tenant-A requests taking at least one prime 429 under the reference router. Token allowances never bind (worst measured 60 s demand is 45% of the tightest tpm), so the subtraction that matters is against rpm and concurrency. cards/workload.json dimensions.fleet_headroom_at_peak.

title: After an attempt is rejected, should the next attempt go to a different provider or wait and try the same one again?
detail: try a different provider first, waiting only when no alternative has room
note: declared default

title: Once a provider is known to be unavailable, when may the router send it real traffic again?
detail: not before the announced end of its unavailability
note: SETTLED BY THE MEASURED TRACE. Outage exposure is not a corner case in this workload: measured against the val schedule, 41.3% of tenant B's val arrivals (286/693, an entire wave: 348.0-437.7 s inside the 300-420 s window) and 15.2% of tenant A's (148/972) land inside an announced prime outage, against 20.0% and 10.8% on train. With retry_grace 8, a policy that re-probes with real traffic burns the loss allowance nine dispatches into a window that lasts 120-150 s. The fleet publishes outage_until, so nothing needs to be inferred. cards/workload.json dimensions.outage_exposure.

title: Should a provider that is not formally unavailable, but has just been refusing or failing requests, be avoided for a while?
detail: yes: a provider that has just been refusing or failing is passed over for a bounded period
note: declared default

title: Does the time left before a request's deadline change what the router does with it?
detail: the deadline changes both the choice of provider and model and how long the request is willing to wait
note: SETTLED BY THE MEASURED TRACE. The two tenants' deadlines are 2,500 ms TTFT (A, 100% of 3,871 rows) and 600,000 ms end-to-end (B, 100% of 2,633 rows), a factor of 240, and the feasible action sets differ in kind, not degree: after one 429 A has 500 ms left, so only prime (ttft_base 400 ms) can still meet the SLO and only under 6,000 prompt tokens, while B's median request can queue 532 s and still finish. Measured: A first-try TTFT feasibility prime 98.05% / value 94.44% / courier 93.72% on val; B solo end-to-end feasibility 99.6-100% at every provider. cards/workload.json dimensions.deadline_feasibility_headroom.

title: What should the router do with a request that can no longer meet its deadline?
detail: serve it anyway, as cheaply as the permitted set allows
note: declared default

title: Is what the router spends bounded by anything other than the traffic itself?
detail: price is weighed against quality on every request, with no hard ceiling
note: declared default

title: Must two replays of the same trace produce the same decisions?
detail: identical decisions on identical input
note: declared default

title: What bounds anything the router remembers between requests?
detail: an explicit size or age limit on everything remembered
note: declared default

title: What must an operator be able to see after a request goes wrong?
detail: which provider and model served it, how many attempts it took, and why each earlier attempt failed
note: declared default

title: Split protocol: fit on train, select on val within 5 evaluations, test untouched
detail: task.md Data protocol: the per-iteration scored measurement runs on trace_tenant{A,B}_train.jsonl. The val split (trace_tenant{A,B}_val.jsonl) may be replayed at most FIVE times across the whole run, each one logged as a numbered val evaluation, and is used only to select among candidates. trace_tenant{A,B}_test.jsonl and matrix_tenant{A,B}_test.jsonl must never be read, replayed, or inspected by any role at any point.
note: Hard constraint from task.md and from the user's invocation. Any read of a *_test.* trace is a protocol violation the auditor must fail the run on.

title: Iteration budget: 30 (user-fixed)
detail: The Step 4 budget question was not asked: the user fixed the budget at 30 iterations in the invocation. Treated as a Standard-class budget for the cold-knowledge-base decision.
note: build (reason: cold, 30 iterations = Standard class): kb-builder runs once in the background against this run's already-cloned reference systems.

title: Environment ceiling, tenant A: U <= 0.669 on train
detail: Achievable ceiling under observable features only (ridge head on req.features['prompt_id']), measured through the real harness with the val outage windows applied: U_A 0.6687 (q 0.7237, $0.0075/req, slo 0.0217). Baseline GenericPolicy(lam=40) on the same train trace: U_A 0.5695. Closable gap +0.099 U. The oracle ceiling that reads req.quality is 0.802 and is forbidden; a candidate above 0.669 on train is reading ground truth. specification/cards/environment.json

title: Environment ceiling, tenant B: U <= 0.462 on train
detail: Achievable ceiling under observable features only, measured through the harness: U_B 0.4631 (q 0.4959, $0.0109/req, slo 0.0). Baseline: U_B 0.3855. Closable gap +0.078 U. Oracle (forbidden) 0.572. Tenant B has no SLO term at all on train: pure quality-per-dollar, and the ceiling SPENDS 6x the baseline. specification/cards/environment.json

title: Tenant A carries an irreducible slo_violation_rate floor of 0.0217 (0.0259 under outage)
detail: 63 of 2899 train requests have prompt_tokens > 126000 = (2500 ms - 400 ms) * 60000 tok/s, prime's best-case prefill, so no provider in the fleet can emit a first token inside the 2.5 s SLO; 20 more fall inside a prime outage window above value's 45000-token budget. No router can score better than 0.0259 on tenant A's SLO term with the val outage schedule. A candidate reporting a lower A SLO rate is mis-accounting.

title: Rate limits are NOT the bound in the scored per-tenant replay
detail: Every train replay (baseline and both ceiling probes, both outage settings, 12 runs) recorded 0 throttles_429 on all three providers. Each tenant's 60 s peak is 34-40% of fleet RPM and 6-11% of fleet TPM. The env card's '19.4% of tenant-A requests throttled' was measured on the MERGED trace; replay_tenants.py replays one tenant at a time, so that contention is absent from the score. Pacing still matters only against courier alone (peak is 160-185% of courier's RPM).

title: Train U is optimistic by ~0.12-0.13 U; only the GAP transfers
detail: The shipped ridge head is fit in-sample on the train matrices (baseline/train_generic.py:81-84). Same policy, same config: baseline U_A 0.5695 train vs 0.4361 val, U_B 0.3855 train vs 0.2702 val. Expect val-equivalent ceilings near A 0.54 / B 0.35. Compare candidates to the baseline on the same split; never quote a train U as a val expectation.

title: Reward-hack lead: a prompt_id -> ground-truth lookup built from the train matrix scores as an oracle on train and is worthless on val/test
detail: make_tenant_traces.py:64-66 splits by sha256(prompt_id)%100 (<60 train, <80 val, else test), so train/val/test prompt ids are disjoint. req.features['prompt_id'] is observable, but joining it against matrix_tenant{A,B}_train.jsonl 'score' (or against req.quality) yields exactly the oracle ceiling on train (U_A 0.802, U_B 0.572) and zero coverage on val/test. Any candidate whose train U approaches the oracle ceiling rather than the achievable ceiling (A 0.669 / B 0.462) must be checked for a quality lookup keyed by prompt_id. The legitimate use of prompt_id is as the key of a GENERALIZING estimator fitted from prompt text, as the shipped ridge head is.

title: Tenant B cannot beat the baseline's SLO clause: the baseline books zero violations
detail: The win criterion is 'quality >= baseline, cost <= baseline, AND SLO-violation rate < baseline'. Measured from the shipped evaluator/benchmark/baseline/generic_baseline_results.json, val.per_tenant.B: the generic baseline completes all 693 tenant-B val requests with slo_violations 0 and slo_violation_rate 0.0000 (p95 latency 185,046 ms against a 600,000 ms deadline). A rate strictly below 0.0 does not exist, so the strict-inequality clause is unsatisfiable for tenant B and the tenant-B win must be argued on quality and cost, with the SLO clause read as 'no worse than'. Confirmed structurally: measured solo end-to-end feasibility is 99.6-100% at every provider and the median tenant-B request has 532 s of queue slack, so zero violations is the expected outcome for any competent policy. The lead should register this reading with the harness owner before the sealed test replay. Evidence: cards/workload.json scored_configuration.tenant_B.
note: Raised in workload mode from the measured val baseline and the measured deadline feasibility.

title: The val outage geometry is unrepresentative: tenant B's second window is dead air
detail: The val outage schedule is two absolute-time windows fixed in env_card.yaml (300,000-420,000 ms and 780,000-930,000 ms) on provider prime. Measured against the tenant-B val trace, wave 1 (348.0-437.7 s) falls entirely inside the FIRST window (286 of 693 arrivals, 41.3%) and wave 2 (1,015.2-1,104.5 s) misses the second window completely (0 arrivals). Tenant A sees 97 then 51 arrivals in the two windows (15.2%). On train the same schedule covers 20.0% of tenant-B arrivals, again all in window 1. The sealed test windows are not absolute: replay_tenants.py:derive_test_outage_windows places two windows of 90-210 s at fractions 0.10-0.35 and 0.55-0.80 of the trace span, so on test an outage can land on ANY wave, including the second. Consequences: (a) val cannot reward or punish handling a second outage for tenant B, so selection on val gives no evidence about it; (b) a policy that special-cases the two literal val windows, or that only ever learns to survive one outage per replay, will fail on test; (c) tenant B's val book is 2 waves against 5 on train, so one mishandled wave moves the val number about 2.5x as much as the train number. Require the outage response to be driven only by the published outage_until in the fleet view, never by wall-clock position, and test it with an outage placed on the second wave. Evidence: cards/workload.json dimensions.outage_exposure and train_vs_val_shift items 3, 4 and 7.
note: Raised in workload mode from the measured arrival-versus-outage overlap on train and val; the test windows were NOT inspected, only the published derivation rule in replay_tenants.py was read.

title: A static model choice for tenant B is inside the train-to-val noise
detail: Measured per-model mean score and cost over the tenant-B matrices: the five best models by static utility (score - 3*cost) lie within 0.011 of each other on each split (train 0.2910 down to 0.2799; val 0.2944 down to 0.2813) while the train-to-val reordering is larger than those gaps: deepseek-r1-0528 goes 1st (0.2910) to 5th (0.2813), gpt-5 2nd to 1st, qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 5th to 3rd; the largest single-model utility shift is 0.0309. Tuning tenant B by picking one model on val is therefore selecting noise inside a five-evaluation budget. What does transfer is per-class routing: the per-class best-model map fitted on TRAIN earns 0.3133 utility on val against 0.2813 for the single train-best model, a +0.0321 gain that survives the split and clears the baseline's 0.2702. difficulty_hint also separates consistently on both splits for tenant B (best-achievable utility 0.13-0.18 in the low quartiles against 0.47-0.50 in the high ones). For contrast tenant A is stable: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 wins on both splits by 0.030-0.055 and every difficulty quartile agrees, while per-class routing adds only +0.0024. Prefer a tenant-B policy keyed on the observable class and difficulty signals over any tuned static choice, and treat a tenant-B val improvement under 0.03 as unresolved. Evidence: cards/workload.json dimensions.quality_cost_landscape, dimensions.observable_signal, train_vs_val_shift items 1 and 2; specification/profiling/{quality_cost,observable_signal}.json.
note: Raised in workload mode from the measured train-versus-val per-model landscape and a train-fitted, val-scored policy transfer check.

title: Operating point: full train replay per tenant, outages active, checked by replay_tenants.py
detail: cards/requirements.json operating_point. The headline score is measured at the FULL scored replay, per tenant, on the TRAIN split, under the env card's outage windows and RPM/TPM/concurrency tiers: tenant A >= 2899 rows of trace_tenantA_train.jsonl at ttft_ms 2500; tenant B >= 1940 rows of trace_tenantB_train.jsonl across >= 5 waves at latency_ms 600000; both specialists covered; --split val so prime is down over 300000-420000 ms and 780000-930000 ms with retry_grace 8; 3 providers / 12 models / rpm {value 420, prime 132, courier 150} / tpm {12M, 3.5M, 5M} / concurrency {96, 32, 48}; <= 512 decide() calls per request; >= 2 replays per configuration for the determinism class. Checker: python3 evaluator/benchmark/replay_tenants.py <trace> <RouterClassPath> --env evaluator/benchmark/env_card.yaml --split val --json, which owns the clock, the fleet, the billing and the SLO accounting and types every violation itself, so it is both scorer and correctness oracle; kept tests additionally pass evaluator/reference_router.py and are mutant-checked with workflow/scripts/validate_test.py --mutant. Pass condition: violation_count 0, requests == completed + shed, and the tenant's book beating GenericPolicy(lam=40, placement='latency') on the same trace and split. The evaluator must write at least one kept test that runs HERE, at full trace length.
note: Chosen per decision log row 19 (fit on train, val reserved for <=5 logged selection evaluations, test never read) and the load measured in cards/environment.json scored_configuration; the shape and objective come from cards/workload.json scored_configuration.

title: Nine required correctness classes carried on the requirements card
detail: cards/requirements.json spec_axes, the correctness.* entries, each grounded file:line in references/task-evaluator and the shipped harness: exactly_once_completion (no lost_request, no double_bill; replay_tenants.py:409, :452), shed_legality (no illegal_shed; :283, a down provider is not headroom :274), substitution_legality (no substitution / unknown_provider / unknown_model; :312, :316, :320), outage_loss_avoidance (no outage_lost past retry_grace 8; :330, :333, env_card.yaml:137), no_mutation (no req_mutation / env_mutation / meter_mutation / bad_bill / router_exception; :235, :359, :453, :455), replay_determinism (identical decisions and books on a second replay; both reference gateways ship an unseeded placement draw), bounded_router_memory (explicit size or age limit on everything kept across requests; up to 512 decide() calls per request, replay.py:35), operator_observability (provider, model, attempt count and each earlier typed failure recoverable after a bad request; nothing self-reported moves the score, :503-:527), and observable_signals_only. Correctness is pass/fail and outside U; these are not traded against the score.
note: The contract the shipped harness already enforces, restated as falsifiable classes so the evaluator can write one kept test per class; hardening mode turns each into a {property, probe, oracle}.

title: Required class: router reads only request-time observable signals, never req.quality or a per-prompt score matrix
detail: cards/requirements.json spec_axes['correctness.observable_signals_only']. The router may read req.features, req.cls, req.prompt_tokens, req.expected_output_tokens, req.max_tokens, req.stream, req.slo, req.model_requested, req.equiv_class, req.downgrade_ok, req.retry_safe, req.session_id, req.prefix_id, now_ms and the fleet view. It may NOT read req.quality (router_interface.py:31), which is the harness's grading key (replay_tenants.py:412), and may NOT join req.features['prompt_id'] against matrix_tenant{A,B}_*.jsonl or any other ground-truth-derived table. Measured separation: observable-feature ceiling U_A 0.669 / U_B 0.462 against the forbidden oracle ceiling U_A 0.802 / U_B 0.572, an information gap of 0.133 and 0.109. The shipped baseline itself stays inside the line (generic_policy.py:42, :60 score from a precomputed prediction head keyed by prompt_id). The specific hack: make_tenant_traces.py:64 splits prompt ids by sha256 into disjoint train/val/test sets, so a prompt_id -> train-matrix score lookup reproduces the oracle ceiling on train and has ZERO coverage on val and test. The legitimate use of prompt_id is as the key of an estimator fitted from prompt text that generalizes to unseen ids, as the shipped ridge head is (train_generic.py:84).
note: Carried forward from decision quality_information_source and decision log row 26 (the environment agent's hack lead). Advisory now because no candidate exists; a candidate whose train U approaches the oracle ceiling rather than the achievable ceiling is to be raised as a defect by the Auditor.

title: Added class: outage response must be driven by published outage_until, not by absolute trace position
detail: cards/properties.json entry outage_loss_avoidance.no_hardcoded_windows. The val outage windows are two LITERAL absolute times in env_card.yaml:138-141 (300000-420000, 780000-930000) while the sealed test windows are derived as span fractions at replay time (replay_tenants.derive_test_outage_windows), so a router with those constants baked in scores on the scored split and collapses on the real one. Probe: shift every t_ms and every outage window by DELTA=1e9 ms and require the decision stream to shift by exactly DELTA and the books (cost, quality, slo, p95, leading_indicators) to be unchanged.
note: Added by the spec-builder in hardening mode; not one of the nine carried classes.

title: Added class: graceful degradation under a provider error storm
detail: cards/properties.json entry failure_degradation.provider_error_storm. Shipped error_rate is 0.002-0.02 (env_card.yaml:86/:109/:132), so the scored replay never exercises a dependency fault. Probe: a scratch copy of the env card with error_rate 0.5 on all three providers, and a second run with 1.0 on prime alone. Oracle: requests == completed + shed, violation_count 0 (no lost_request/unserviceable/router_exception/harness_hang), decides inside the 512/request budget; on the prime-only run every request completes. Catches the realistic defect of permanently blacklisting a provider after one 503.
note: Added by the spec-builder in hardening mode; production-checklist lens 'failure modes and degradation'.

title: Thresholds chosen in hardening mode: oracle-ceiling screen and memory growth tolerance
detail: Two numbers I picked, both recorded so they can be argued with. (1) observable_signals_only.no_oracle_ceiling fails a candidate at U_A > 0.735 or U_B > 0.517: the MIDPOINTS between the measured observable ceiling (0.669/0.462, decision rows 20-21) and the forbidden oracle ceiling (0.802/0.572, row 26). Midpoint, not the ceiling itself, so an honestly better observable policy keeps a full half-gap of headroom. Measured: ReferenceRouter books U_A 0.1477, U_B 0.3113. (2) bounded_router_memory fails at objects(4N)-objects(N) > max(2000, 0.25*objects(N)) on a 4x-length trace with a fresh id space. Measured: ReferenceRouter (1 object, 48 B) flat at both checkpoints; a one-record-per-decide copy goes (1633, 131042) -> (4933, 455947).
note: Spec-builder, hardening mode. Both thresholds are measured against the shipped ReferenceRouter, not guessed.

title: operator_observability has no output channel in the shipped interface: needs a two-method contract extension or goes advisory
detail: correctness.operator_observability requires an operator to recover provider, model, attempt count and each typed failure after a request goes wrong, but router_interface.py defines no output channel and the shipped evaluator/reference_router.py -- which task.md makes the pass oracle for EVERY test -- cannot satisfy the positive half. cards/properties.json entry operator_observability therefore names a minimal extension: incident(req_id) -> {provider, model, attempts, errors:[(kind, now_ms)]} | None with a declared retention bound, validated against a ReferenceRouter+incident() reference the evaluator writes from the spec, with a stale-record mutant. The negative half (nothing the router reports moves the harness books; no meter_mutation/env_mutation/bad_bill) is testable against the shipped reference as-is. LEAD DECISION NEEDED: adopt the extension and require it of both delivered routers, or record this class advisory with this reason.
note: Spec-builder, hardening mode. Flagged rather than papered over: a test that requires incident() would fail the shipped trusted reference and be rejected by validate_test.py.

title: Headline is U; the win claim is the three-clause gate
detail: task.md states BOTH: 'Tune against this metric, fixed before the first evaluation: U = mean_quality - 1.0*slo_violation_rate - 3.0*cost_usd_per_request' AND a per-tenant win condition of quality >= baseline, cost <= baseline, slo_violation_rate < baseline. The planner found these disagree: the U-maximal router spends 1.7x (A) and 8.7x (B) the baseline's cost gate.
note: RULING (lead, no human available): follow task.md exactly, which means both. The synthesis loop optimises the CONSTRAINED problem: maximise U subject to quality >= q_base AND cost <= c_base AND slo < slo_base, per tenant. U alone orders candidates inside the feasible set; a candidate outside it is not a win however high its U. Every scored evaluation reports BOTH rows: the gated row (the win claim) and the unconstrained-U row (the measured ceiling, reported as context). lam is the shadow price on the cost clause and is calibrated on train, never on val.

title: Shipped ridge head is in bounds
detail: evaluator/benchmark/artifacts/generic_predictions.json is the Qwen2.5-0.5B + per-model Ridge estimator the shipped baseline reads (generic_policy.py:42,:60).
note: RULING (lead): in bounds, verified not assumed. baseline/train_generic.py:24 SPLITS=('train','val') with an assert at :34 refusing any other split; :81-:92 fit_on = merged tenantA+tenantB TRAIN matrices; :107 predicts train+val prompt ids only, with test predictions extended from the saved heads by the harness owner at sealed-eval time. So it is a generalizing estimator fit on train, not a label lookup, and it is the SAME information the baseline has: using it compares policy against policy. Legitimate use of prompt_id; distinct from the forbidden prompt_id -> ground-truth-matrix join. The auditor is told this up front. Fallback if it is ever ruled out: plan.md candidate C5 (head-free class x difficulty table, measured A ~0.53 / B ~0.31, below baseline).

title: operator_observability: adopt incident(req_id) on both routers
detail: The answered property what_an_operator_can_see requires provider, model, attempt count and each earlier typed failure to be recoverable after a bad request, but the shipped Router interface has no output channel, so evaluator/reference_router.py cannot satisfy the positive half.
note: RULING (lead): adopt the extension rather than drop an answered requirement. Both delivered routers expose incident(req_id) -> {provider, model, attempts, errors} | None with a declared retention bound (this is also what bounded_router_memory bounds). The evaluator (correctness mode) writes the trusted reference for it as ReferenceRouter + incident(), derived from the specification, and validates the test against that. The negative half (nothing the router reports moves the harness books) is validated against the shipped reference unchanged. Closed by the kept test for operator_observability.

title: Delivery convention: routers.json names the class per tenant
detail: Two artifacts are delivered (one specialist Router per tenant) but nothing fixed how the suite and the harness learn which class serves which tenant.
note: RULING (lead): the delivered implementation directory carries routers.json = {"A": "<module>.<Class>", "B": "<module>.<Class>"}, resolved relative to $SKYDISCOVER_IMPL, with a TENANT class attribute as fallback. Every test, the benchmark harness and the delivery hook resolve the pair through it. The bootstrap coding agent writes it; the planner records it in the brief.

title: env_card / predictions sha256 on the cards do not match the shipped files
detail: cards/requirements.json operating_point.params.providers.note pins env_card.yaml at sha256 14b1d5b1ac020b7e1b8d8d5d331fae948cd125f13da598b263f586ff9e447b16, and evaluator/benchmark/baseline/generic_baseline_results.json artifacts.env_card carries the same digest. The shipped skydiscover/synthesize/examples/llm-router/evaluator/benchmark/env_card.yaml actually hashes 04a63812f54082abdd2dc4b4d4c865d0bb27cb0719315325cdfbb917ec0135c4. The same file also points artifacts.predictions at evaluator/benchmark/.data/traces/generic_predictions.json (sha c1a8b5af...), a path that does not exist; the artifact the baseline actually loads is evaluator/benchmark/artifacts/generic_predictions.json (sha 5980ac97fc4009c9ede3f4a95a174aeca3fd133b6a1c45f4db6598448bb96bed). So the provenance digests on the cards are stale labels for the files the harness really reads.
note: Not a scoring problem as far as iteration 1 can tell: re-measuring GenericPolicy(lam=40, placement='latency') in-process against the shipped card and artifact reproduces the registered baseline row EXACTLY on both tenants (A q 0.6212 / $0.004362 / slo 0.0386 / U 0.5695; B q 0.3907 / $0.001746 / slo 0.0 / U 0.3855), which is what the pass condition is gated on. Logged so the digests get refreshed rather than silently trusted, and so a later card edit cannot hide behind an already-wrong pin. The run's own vendored copies under synthesis/evaluator/benchmark/vendor/ are byte-identical to the shipped files.

title: Iteration budget REVISED: 30 -> 10 (user directive, resumed run)
detail: The user reduced the iteration budget from 30 (decision row 'iteration-budget') to 10 when resuming this run. Reason, stated by the user: the previous session was killed by an API session limit after ~85 minutes WITHOUT completing a single scored iteration -- tests and mutants were on disk but the leaderboard and checkpoints were empty -- so the budget is cut to reach a scored, checkpointed candidate within one session. The run therefore used 10 iterations, not 30; report.md states 'k of 10'. Consequences: (a) the 30-iteration schedule in synthesis/plan.md '## Budget' is void and the planner must re-timetable C0 -> C1/C2 inside 10; (b) priority order is SCORE FIRST -- one candidate measured and checkpointed before any iteration is spent on refinement; (c) a measured result that misses the baseline is a valid outcome and is reported as a miss, per task.md 'report misses as misses'. UNCHANGED by this directive: the five-evaluation val budget, fit-on-train/select-on-val, and the rule that trace_tenant{A,B}_test.jsonl and matrix_tenant{A,B}_test.jsonl are never read.
